verdict.line: You lose if you walk into his Parrrley range before level 3; you win if you land E and force an extended melee trade where stacked Hemorrhage and the Guillotine execute outclass his sustain.

brief.thesis: Darius has no gap-closer or ranged tool until E (Apprehend) comes online at level 3, while Gangplank's Q (Parrrley, range 625) lets him poke and refund mana on kills without ever entering melee — this is why Gangplank holds lane advantage. Once Darius pulls him in with E or commits with R, Gangplank's only answer is W (Remove Scurvy, cooldown 22/21/20/19/18s), a single cleanse-and-heal that cannot out-sustain five stacks of Hemorrhage and a true-damage Guillotine — which is why the solo-kill edge flips to Darius.

theirWindow.what: He fires Parrrley for free poke and gold, and his Grog-Soaked Blade poison keeps ticking magic damage on top of any auto he lands. Don't trade at range — you have nothing that reaches him back.

yourWindow.when: after E lands and his W is down
yourWindow.what: Chain autos and W (Crippling Strike) to slow him in place, stack Hemorrhage, and finish with R once he's near max stacks — without W up he has no cleanse and no heal to answer it.

start.why: Measured 52.5% win rate over 200 games and fits the aggressive, solo-kill-favoured shape of this matchup — you want the extra damage to end trades fast once you're in range, not to out-sustain his poke.

boots.why: 80.7% pick rate and 48.2% win rate over 371 games; the flat auto-attack damage reduction blunts both his Parrrley autos and the Grog-Soaked Blade poison stacking on you.

core.why: The active gives you a burst of speed to close the gap his Q poke otherwise denies you — this path hits 57.6% win rate over 59 games.
Builds a slow on hit so once you've pulled him in with E he can't walk away between W cleanses.
Converts incoming damage to a delayed heal, which directly answers the Grog-Soaked Blade poison ticking on you through extended trades.

situational.when: he starts focusing you down with burst once he has gold from early Q kills
his poison and any magic damage sources are chunking you faster than Death's Dance can heal back
you need the slow-on-hit and waveclear more than the gap-close from Youmuu's

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramps bonus AD and healing the longer a fight goes, which rewards exactly the extended melee trades you're forced into after an E pull — and the healing offsets the Grog-Soaked Blade poison tick.

summoners.why: This page measures the highest win rate of the three run (51.4% over the sample). Ignite's execute and healing reduction punish the exact window where Gangplank tries to W (Remove Scurvy) his way out of your all-in.

playing.title: Don't walk up before level 3
playing.detail: Without E you have no way to close the distance on his 625-range Q — every approach before level 3 is a free poke for him.

playing.title: Pull, don't walk
playing.detail: Open every trade with E (Apprehend) to close the gap in one motion instead of eating Parrrley on the way in.

playing.title: Check his W before committing
playing.detail: Remove Scurvy is on a 22/21/20/19/18s cooldown — if it's down, your E all-in has no cleanse to break through.

playing.title: Stack before you swing R
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine's true damage scales with Hemorrhage stacks, so land Q and autos first and save R to close the kill.

playing.title: Chase resets after a kill
playing.detail: R's cooldown refreshes to 6 seconds on a killing blow — use that window to immediately threaten a second target in a skirmish.

playing.title: Respect the poison clock in long fights
playing.detail: Grog-Soaked Blade's poison damage scales with his level, so don't assume a trade that was even at level 3 is still even at level 9.

playing.title: Fight him whenever he's in your range
playing.detail: Every exchange inside melee range is one he has to burn W or lose a summoner spell to escape — take those fights.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, item paths, runes, and summoner spells above are measured from real games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning for why those numbers look the way they do is this brief's own analysis.

stats.opponentTip: Fight Gangplank whenever he stands in your range to either kill him or get a Summoner’s Spell from him. Be careful of his Graps of the Undying + (Q) combo.
